info.title: Support Ticket SLA API
info.description: REST API for the Support Ticket SLA system. Authenticated endpoints expect a JWT in the `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header.

post.description: Self-registration always creates a **customer**. Admin and agent accounts are created by administrators.

post.summary: Log in and obtain a JWT
post.description: Get a JWT via given credentials.
Log the user out (Invalidate the token).
Accepts a valid token, or an expired one still inside the refresh window (JWT_REFRESH_TTL). The old token is blacklisted.

get.description:
Ticket numbers for the logged-in user, counted over the tickets they may see: customers their own tickets, agents the tickets assigned to them plus the unassigned queue, admins all tickets.

`open_tickets`, `unassigned`, `critical`, `sla_breached` and `sla_approaching` count **active** tickets only (open, in progress, waiting for customer). `resolved` and `closed` count finished tickets.

**Staff only** (agents and admins): `sla_breached`, `sla_approaching` and `by_agent`. Customers do not get these keys. For an agent, `by_agent` only contains themselves.

by_agent.description: Staff only. Active tickets per assigned agent, busiest first

get.description: List the categories a ticket can be filed under.

post.summary: Assign a ticket to an agent
post.description: Admin only. Gives the ticket to an active support agent, replacing the current one if there is one. The agent does not have to be marked available. Resolved and closed tickets cannot be assigned.

agent_id.description: User id of an active agent

post.description: Agents only. Takes an unassigned ticket for yourself. If two agents accept at the same time, exactly one succeeds and the other gets 409. Accepting a ticket that is already yours succeeds without changing anything.

get.description: Every file on the ticket and on its replies that you may see. Files on internal notes are only listed for staff. Each entry has a `download_url`.

post.description:
Attaches files to the ticket itself (to attach to a reply, send them with the reply instead). Same people as replying: the owning customer, the assigned agent, admins. Closed tickets return 409.

Limits: up to 5 files per request, 5 MB each. Allowed types: jpg, jpeg, png, gif, webp, pdf, txt, log, csv, docx, xlsx. The file content is checked, not only its name. Files are stored privately and served only through `download_url`.

get.description: Downloads one file. Requires the Bearer token like every other endpoint (a plain browser link will not work: fetch it with the header and save the response). The file is always sent as a download with `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, never displayed inline. A file on an internal note returns 404 to customers, as if it did not exist.

parameters.name: attachment
parameters.description: Attachment id (uuid) from the attachment list

get.description: Every ticket the current user may see, newest first. Customers see their own tickets, agents see tickets assigned to them plus the unassigned queue, admins see all.

post.description:
Creates a ticket with status `open` and a new unique number such as `TKT-2026-000001`. `priority` defaults to `medium`.

**Who can create:** customers only. Agents and admins get **403**; they work on tickets customers raise. The ticket is owned by the customer who creates it and starts unassigned.

description.example: I get an error after entering my password.

get.description: Open, in-progress and waiting-for-customer tickets, earliest SLA deadline first (tickets without a deadline last). Any logged-in, enabled user may call it; results are filtered by role: customers see their own tickets, agents see tickets assigned to them plus the unassigned queue, admins see all.

Resolved and closed tickets, most recently updated first. Any logged-in, enabled user may call it; results are filtered by role: customers see their own tickets, agents see tickets assigned to them plus the unassigned queue, admins see all.

200.description: A page of resolved or closed tickets

patch.description: Send only the fields to change. Customers may edit `subject`, `description` and `category_id` of their own ticket while it is still `open`, and may not send `priority`. Agents can edit tickets assigned to them, admins any ticket. Closed tickets cannot be edited.

**Who can do what**

| Role | May change status of | To which status |
|------|----------------------|-----------------|
| Admin | any ticket | any allowed move (table below) |
| Agent | only tickets assigned to them (an unassigned ticket must be accepted first) | any allowed move |
| Customer | only their own tickets | `closed` only |

Anyone else gets **403**. Role and ownership are checked first, then the move itself.

**Allowed moves** (anything else returns **409**, including sending the current status again)

| From | To |
|------|----|
| `open` | `in_progress`, `waiting_for_customer`, `resolved`, `closed` |
| `in_progress` | `waiting_for_customer`, `resolved`, `closed` |
| `waiting_for_customer` | `in_progress`, `resolved`, `closed` |
| `resolved` | `in_progress` (reopen), `closed` |
| `closed` | none, `closed` is final |

**Side effects**
- `resolved` sets `resolved_at`; `closed` sets `closed_at`.
- Reopening a resolved ticket (`in_progress`) clears `resolved_at`.
- Only `open`, `in_progress` and `waiting_for_customer` tickets are active, so only they count towards the SLA.

Shortcuts: `PATCH /tickets/{ticket}/resolve` and `PATCH /tickets/{ticket}/close`.
Shortcut for setting the status to `resolved`. Agents (assigned) and admins only.
Shortcut for setting the status to `closed` (final). The ticket owner, the assigned agent and admins may close a ticket.

get.description: The conversation on a ticket, oldest first. Customers see replies only; **internal agent notes are never included for customers**. Staff (the assigned agent, or any agent while the ticket is unassigned, and admins) see replies and internal notes, marked with `is_internal`. Returns 404 "not found" when the ticket has no visible replies yet.

post.summary: Reply to a ticket or add an internal note
post.description:
Adds a reply to the ticket, optionally with files. Who may reply: the customer who owns the ticket, the agent it is assigned to, and admins. An agent must accept an unassigned ticket before replying.

Set `is_internal` to `true` to write an **internal note**: only staff may do this (a customer gets 403), and the note and its files are never shown to customers.

Send JSON for text only, or `multipart/form-data` to attach files (`attachments[]`). Files are validated by real content, not just name; see the `attachments` field. Closed tickets return 409.

is_internal.description: `true`/`1` = internal note, staff only. Default false.

attachments.description: Up to 5 files, 5 MB each. Allowed: jpg, jpeg, png, gif, webp, pdf, txt, log, csv, docx, xlsx.

Keyword.name: q
Keyword.description: Search text (2 to 100 characters). Matches anywhere in the ticket number, subject or description. Not case sensitive.

CategoryFilter.name: category_id
CategoryFilter.description: Only tickets in this category (id from GET /api/categories)

AssignedToFilter.name: assigned_to
AssignedToFilter.description: Only tickets assigned to this agent (user id). Cannot be combined with `unassigned`.

UnassignedFilter.name: unassigned
UnassignedFilter.description: `true` = only tickets nobody has taken yet. Cannot be combined with `assigned_to`.

CustomerFilter.name: customer_id
CustomerFilter.description: Only tickets created by this customer (user id)

CreatedFrom.name: created_from
CreatedFrom.description: Created on or after this day (YYYY-MM-DD, UTC)

CreatedTo.name: created_to
CreatedTo.description: Created on or before this day, the whole day included (YYYY-MM-DD, UTC). Not before `created_from`.

TicketSort.name: sort
TicketSort.description: Order of the results. `sla_deadline`: earliest SLA deadline first, tickets without one last. `created_asc`: oldest first. `created_desc`: newest first. Replaces the default order of the endpoint.

SlaFilter.name: sla
SlaFilter.description: Only ACTIVE tickets in this SLA state: `within`, `approaching` (most of the SLA time used) or `breached` (past the deadline). Tickets without a deadline match none.
